output.title: Synthetic test data: use it to decide, not to decorate
output.body:
Synthetic test data is useful when it helps you decide faster. It is less useful when it becomes a side project that delays the first real workflow test.

For a small business, the bounded question is simple: are you using synthetic data because you need privacy or scale, or because nobody has tried the workflow on real records yet? If the pilot is a repeatable task like invoice handling or customer inquiry triage, start smaller: take a limited real-data subset, write clear rules, and keep a human approval step for money movement or other high-risk decisions.

Bareni’s accounts-payable demo is a useful boundary case. It uses entirely synthetic data to show the mechanics: text-based extraction, arithmetic checks, duplicate blocking, and audit records. But it also has limits. The default route uses pre-extracted files, and PDF/scan ingestion and OCR are not implemented. So it demonstrates control logic, not readiness for every invoice pile.

My practical next step: pick one workflow, one approval rule, and one small batch of real records. Then ask whether synthetic data is solving a real testing problem, or just postponing the moment you learn what the workflow actually needs.
